name: Minimally invasive transpsoas approach (L2–L4)
corridor: 3–4 cm lateral cut over the disc, split the three abdominal-wall layers without cautery, finger into retroperitoneal fat, then a 3–4 cm psoas split over the disc with a tubular localizer

positioning.text: Position so fluoroscopy can mark the target disc. L5–S1 cannot be reached.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the disc on the skin exactly in the line of the target.

incision.text: Make a 3–4 cm cut in the direction of the disc (longer if more than one level).

superficial_interval.text: Split external oblique, then internal oblique (fibers roughly perpendicular), then open transversalis fascia carefully. Do not use cautery; it can injure superficial sensory nerves. Repair a peritoneal tear immediately with absorbable suture on a blunt tapered needle.

deep_interval.text: Use a finger to find retroperitoneal fat and follow psoas fibers without wandering anterior or posterior. After x-ray confirmation, split psoas 3–4 cm over the disc and place a tubular localizer, checked on AP and lateral views. Neuromonitoring is recommended for a transpsoas split; temporary iliopsoas pain and nerve-root lesions are common.

layers.text: Skin, three abdominal-wall layers, retroperitoneal fat, psoas split, then the L2–L4 disc.

structures_at_risk.text: The peritoneum, lumbar plexus within psoas, and superficial abdominal-wall sensory nerves are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Cautery in the abdominal wall, wandering off psoas fibers, and a transpsoas split without neuromonitoring are the danger zones.

retraction_hazards.text: Muscles are split, not cut, so they are not sutured; close fascia only.

exposure.text: A retroperitoneal minimally invasive corridor ideal for cage insertion at L2–L4.

limitations.text: Cannot reach L5–S1. A lumbotomy that retracts psoas posteriorly rather than splitting it is the alternative.

indications.text: Used for minimally invasive lateral cage insertion at L2–L4.

closure.text: Close fascia and the wound in layers; do not suture the split muscles.

complications.text: Complications include peritoneal injury with organ damage or hernia, iliopsoas pain, and mostly temporary nerve-root lesions after a psoas split.

procedure_applications.condition: An L2–L4 cage is inserted through a lateral transpsoas window; L5–S1 cannot be reached
